name: O-Toro Tour
feelExpand: Firm hexagonal co-poly with high feedback transmission and a low, flat launch.

name: Caviar
feelExpand: Tight, low-powered response with a narrow launch window and predictable placement.

name: Vamos
feelExpand: Hexagonal profile over the A5 polymer — added edge bite and a higher launch angle than the round base string.

name: Cash
feelExpand: Firm round co-poly with clear feedback; spin from snapback rather than edge bite.

name: A5
feelExpand: Round profile relying on snapback rather than edge bite; clear feedback with a predictable launch angle.

name: A5 Infrared
feelExpand: Softened 1.20 version of the A5 polymer — deeper pocketing and more launch, less of A5's firmness.

name: O-Toro
feelExpand: Dampened response compared to the Tour variant, with less vibration at contact.

name: O-Toro Octa
feelExpand: Sharper ball response than the standard version, with less energy absorption on contact.

name: O-Toro Spin
feelExpand: Increased string-to-ball friction for higher spin rates and better bite on the ball.

name: O-Toro Snap
feelExpand: Ultra-slick round co-poly built for snapback; medium stiffness, flat trajectory.

name: Wasabi
feelExpand: Unusually comfortable for a string with angular cross-section.

name: Toro Toro
feelExpand: Deeper ball dwell time than the standard version in this lineup.

name: Enso Pro (Carbon)
feelExpand: The carbon-coloured version plays noticeably firmer and more direct than the pink variant.

name: Snapper
feelExpand: Octagonal profile at low stiffness — bite-driven spin with a soft, damped contact.

name: Super Toro
feelExpand: Budget hex co-poly with a softer formula and a simpler construction than the O-Toro family.

name: Truffle X
feelExpand: Advanced polymer material with exceptionally low stiffness.

name: O-Toro Snap Tour Flex
feelExpand: Stiff, low-friction surface that keeps shots predictable with a muted, efficient response.

name: Tour Bite
feelExpand: Responsive feel with energy return and clear ball feedback.

name: Confidential
feelExpand: Predictable response with excellent directional accuracy.

name: Confidential Soft
feelExpand: Deeper ball dwell time than the stiffer version, with a more arm-friendly response.

name: Hyper-G
feelExpand: Square co-poly with strong vibration damping; feedback through the handle is quieter than its stiffness suggests.

name: Mach-10
feelExpand: Ball sits in the stringbed briefly; feedback is softened.

name: Tour Bite Soft
feelExpand: Deeper ball dwell time than the standard version in this lineup.

name: Hyper-G Soft
feelExpand: Lower stiffness than the standard version; more ball pocketing.

name: Revolution
feelExpand: Hexagonal co-poly with a harder contact than typical polyester; snappy response with minimal pocketing.

name: TB Diamond Rough
feelExpand: String surface texture grips the ball for enhanced spin generation.

name: Hyper-G Round
feelExpand: Stretchy stringbed that holds the ball longer on contact for added dwell time.

name: Barb Wire
feelExpand: Twisted construction with very high surface friction; medium stiffness.

name: Outlast
feelExpand: Consistent, predictable stringbed response with no surprises across the full swing range.

name: Vanquish (Multi)
feelExpand: Soft stringbed that absorbs and returns energy for comfortable power.

name: Poly Tour Spin
feelExpand: Flat trajectory with a firm, penetrating response.

name: Poly Tour Strike
feelExpand: Round co-poly with a firm, penetrating response and the best tension hold in the Yonex range.

name: Poly Tour Pro
feelExpand: Reliable dwell time on the ball for consistent shotmaking.

name: Poly Tour Rev
feelExpand: Stiff stringbed with muted vibration and reduced feedback.

name: Poly Tour Drive
feelExpand: Medium-firm pentagonal co-poly with clear feedback, sold at an entry-level price.

name: Poly Tour Force
feelExpand: More powerful than average while still transmitting ball feedback.

name: Poly Tour Fire
feelExpand: Silicone coating adds power and dampening to the stringbed.

name: Poly Tour Air
feelExpand: Softest Yonex poly — cushioned contact, high arc over the net.

name: Poly Tour Tough
feelExpand: Durability-oriented round co-poly: low static stiffness, low energy return — absorbs pace rather than adding it.

name: Tour Super 850 (Multi)
feelExpand: Soft, cushioned feel designed to reduce impact shock and protect the arm.

name: Vivo
feelExpand: Firm hexagonal co-poly with clear feedback; 100/100 tension maintenance on Racketpedia.

name: Sync
feelExpand: Excellent feedback for shot placement with a controlled feel.

name: Zero
feelExpand: Stiff stringbed with muted vibration and reduced feedback.

name: SLAP (Ltd. Edition)
feelExpand: Zero-based formula with a livelier, softer profile. Limited edition.

name: Tour Sniper
feelExpand: Pre-stretched pentagonal co-poly; damped, control-oriented feel with minimal break-in.

name: Soldier
feelExpand: Seven-sided profile with a micro-particle abrasive surface; requires 2–3 sessions before snapback settles in.

name: Tour M8
feelExpand: Sits between Alpha and Tour Sniper in stiffness; a coating that gives a distinctive, loud contact sound.

name: Alpha
feelExpand: Soft, cushioned feel that prioritizes arm comfort.

name: Aspera Triplum
feelExpand: Triple-spin construction: square shape, abrasive surface and diamond indentations, on a soft formula.

name: Game Changer
feelExpand: Combines power with above-average spin generation.

name: Paradox Pro
feelExpand: Classic co-poly character with firm, traditional feel.

name: Tour Mako
feelExpand: Very soft (0.45 kg/mm) round co-poly with an abrasive surface and non-metallic additives.

name: Tour Mako Short Fin
feelExpand: Hexagonal edges combined with a rough coating for aggressive ball-grabbing spin.

name: Irukandji
feelExpand: Rectangular-round cross string built to add snapback without notching the mains.

name: ALU Power
feelExpand: Aluminum-coated polyester. The benchmark control-oriented co-poly — the ATP standard for two decades. Smooth response, exceptional consistency.

name: ALU Power Rough
feelExpand: ALU Power with a textured surface. Same 1.05 kg/mm stiffness and tension stability, with notably more spin potential.

name: ALU Power Soft
feelExpand: Lower-stiffness sister to ALU Power. Notable dwell time without going fully soft. For arms that find standard ALU Power too direct.

name: ALU Power Spin
feelExpand: Pentagonal-shaped sister to ALU Power. Slightly less smooth feel, much more spin access. The shape engages the ball positively at contact.

name: ALU Power Feel
feelExpand: Thinner-gauge ALU Power tuned for added feel and spin response. Slightly more lively than the standard line.

name: 4G
feelExpand: Stiffer than ALU Power with exceptional tension maintenance — the longest-lasting playability of any Luxilon. For pros who want the firmest possible reference response.

name: 4G Rough
feelExpand: 4G with surface texture for spin. Same exceptional tension maintenance, with significantly more grip on the ball.

name: 4G Soft
feelExpand: 4G's tension stability with reduced stiffness. Sits between ALU Power Soft and standard 4G in feel.

name: Element
feelExpand: IRIS-fiber co-poly. The most comfort-oriented Luxilon mainline string — designed for players who want poly control without the bite.

name: Adrenaline
feelExpand: Pentagonal cross-section optimized for spin without sacrificing the firm Luxilon response. Plays similarly to ALU Power Spin with slightly more aggressive shape.

name: M2 Pro
feelExpand: Multifilament-like response in a co-poly construction. Aimed at players transitioning from natural gut or syn-gut who want some control without losing comfort.

name: Eco Power
feelExpand: Bio-sourced polyester (~60% renewable feedstock). Similar playability to ALU Power Soft in a more sustainable construction. Marketed as a bridge between performance and environmental responsibility.

name: Big Hitter Black 7
feelExpand: Heptagonal (7-sided) co-poly. The most distinctive spin profile in the Tourna line — sharper edges than typical pentagonals. A favorite among NCAA and lower-tour pros.

name: Big Hitter Blue Rough
feelExpand: Textured polyester aimed at competitive juniors and college players. A blue alternative to ALU Power Rough at a friendlier price point.

name: Big Hitter Silver Rough
feelExpand: A softer-formula sister to Big Hitter Black 7. Same brand, friendlier feel — for arms that find typical co-polys too direct.

name: Pro 16
feelExpand: No-frills round co-poly. Tournament-grade durability at an entry-level price. Workhorse string for high-school and club players.

name: Quasi-Gut Armor
feelExpand: Multifilament with armored coating for durability. Aimed at recreational players who want gut-like comfort without the cost or maintenance.

name: Pro Tour
feelExpand: Nylon synthetic gut with wrap construction — very soft, beginner-oriented; occasionally used as a budget cross.
